low_gods.description: Nuada stands advancing from a battlefield turned throne-ground, a towering, broad-shouldered Celtic king with weathered human features and bronze-toned skin, clad in heavy ceremonial armor chased with lunar silver, his flawless silver hand glowing with sovereign runes as it grips a great sword held point-down in judgment; his posture is unyielding yet restrained, his eyes calm with earned authority, and behind him shattered banners rise and reassemble as if reality itself acknowledges his right to rule, while his aura radiates a cold, noble gravity that steadies armies and silences dissent, proclaiming him a king not born perfect, but reforged through sacrifice into legitimacy.
low_gods.lore: First High King of the Tuatha Dé Danann, Nuada-No-Ken earned his throne through wisdom, not birthright. When he lost his right arm defending Skydrift from the Fomorian invasion, ancient law declared no imperfect king could rule. He stepped down without complaint, proving his devotion to law over power. His silver arm, crafted by the physician Dian Cecht, became stronger than flesh, symbolizing that true strength comes from accepting limitation and adaptation. When he reclaimed his throne, he ruled with even greater wisdom, having learned both the weight of the crown and the humility of the commoner.
low_gods.appearance: A regal warrior-king with silver hair and eyes, his right arm gleaming with intricate silver plates that move like living metal. Wears a crown of intertwined swords and torcs.
low_gods.ascension_story: Rose from mortal kingship to divinity after his second reign, when he voluntarily abdicated a second time to prevent civil war, proving his commitment to Skydrift's peace over personal power. The collective gratitude of the people elevated him to godhood.

unique_abilities.name: Airgetlám (Silver Hand)
unique_abilities.effect: His silver arm can sense truth in speech, detect corruption in systems, and heal wounds of injustice when placed on them
unique_abilities.cooldown: Continuous, but drains his divine essence with heavy use

unique_abilities.name: Claidheamh Soluis (Sword of Light)
unique_abilities.effect: His sword reveals hidden truths and cuts through deception, but cannot harm the innocent
unique_abilities.cooldown: Must be drawn only for just causes

unique_abilities.name: Kingly Sacrifice
unique_abilities.effect: Can temporarily transfer his royal authority to another, making them the legitimate ruler until he reclaims it
unique_abilities.cooldown: Once per reign, risk of permanent transfer if recipient proves worthy

low_gods.current_role: Judge of kings, arbiter of succession disputes, patron of wounded warriors.
duties: Adjudicating royal succession conflicts
Testing would-be rulers for selflessness
Healing warriors who sacrificed limbs in battle
Maintaining the ancient laws of kingship
Teaching that true authority comes from service
sacred_items: Airgetlám (the living silver arm)
Claidheamh Soluis (Sword of Light that reveals truth)
Crown of Abdication (grants authority only to those who don't seek it)
Scale of Royal Sacrifice (weighs a ruler's personal losses against their people's gain)

rivals: Deities of absolute power without responsibility
students: Wounded kings learning to rule differently

weaknesses: Cannot wield his sword for personal gain
Bound by the very laws he upholds
His silver arm grows heavy when lies are spoken in his presence
Cannot refuse a legitimate challenge to his judgments

low_gods.name: Goibniu-No-Kaji, The Immortal Smith
low_gods.god_of: Smith god whose weapons always hit, whose beer grants immortality. Hosts otherworld feast.
low_gods.description: Goibniu looms within a forge that opens into a mythic hall of endless revelry, a massively built Celtic god with soot-darkened skin and a powerful human face split by a craftsman's grin, his noble armor layered with forge-aprons and glowing rivets, muscles corded like wrought iron as he strikes a star-metal anvil mid-swing; sparks freeze into weapons midair while golden ale flows through the floor like veins, warriors laughing in eternal health behind him, and his aura is a roaring warmth of creation and fellowship that binds gods together as kin, revealing him as the immortal architect not only of weapons, but of unbreakable unity.
low_gods.lore: Goibniu-No-Kaji is one of the three gods of craftsmanship (with Luchta the wright and Creidhne the metalworker) who supply the Tuatha Dé Danann with their weapons and wonders. His forge at Murias produces not just weapons but the very concept of 'fit for purpose.' During the Second Battle of Moytura, he worked tirelessly, creating swords that never dulled and spears that never missed, while his brother gods repaired damaged weapons instantly. His feast of immortality isn't just about eternal life—it's about preserving the bonds of fellowship that make life worth living eternally.
low_gods.appearance: A massive, muscular smith covered in soot and glowing embers, with forearms like tree trunks and eyes that spark like struck flint. Always wears a leather apron covered in tool marks.
low_gods.ascension_story: Was already divine when he arrived with the Tuatha Dé Danann, but achieved his current status by forging the Unity Chalice—a drinking horn that, when passed among warriors, makes them brothers regardless of birth. This act prevented a civil war among the gods.

unique_abilities.name: Fís Baile (City Vision)
unique_abilities.effect: Can see the perfect form of any object before forging it, including its entire history and potential futures
unique_abilities.cooldown: One perfect vision per project

unique_abilities.name: Beoir Neamhbhásmhar (Immortality Ale)
unique_abilities.effect: His specially brewed ale grants temporary immortality and perfect health to those who drink it in fellowship
unique_abilities.cooldown: Only effective during his feast; effects last until the next feast

unique_abilities.name: Comhghuaillíocht (Alliance Forging)
unique_abilities.effect: Can create objects that symbolically bind groups together, making them function as a unified whole
unique_abilities.cooldown: The object must be accepted by all parties

low_gods.current_role: Armorer of the gods, host of the Feast of Immortality, patron of craft guilds.
duties: Forging divine weapons and artifacts
Brewing the ale for the Feast of Immortality
Teaching master craftsmanship
Maintaining the forges of Murias
Settling disputes between craft guilds
sacred_items: The Anvil of Destiny (shapes fate as well as metal)
Unity Chalice (creates bonds between drinkers)
Ever-Full Ale Keg
Hammer of Perfect Strikes (never misses its mark)

rivals: Those who use tools for destruction without creation

weaknesses: Cannot create anything without a clear purpose
His ale loses power if drunk alone
Bound to complete any forging commission accepted in good faith
Vulnerable to the corrosion of ingratitude

low_gods.name: Dian Cecht-No-Chiyu, The Healing Waters
low_gods.god_of: Healer god whose well restores dead to life if placed in it. Killed own son out of jealousy of better healer.
low_gods.description: Dian Cecht stands at the edge of a moonlit well that reflects both life and death, a tall, imposing Celtic god with sharp human features and pale, marble-toned skin, wrapped in austere healer's robes reinforced with ritual armor plates etched in medical sigils, his hands glowing with icy-blue restorative power even as shadows of broken bodies and resurrected warriors drift behind him; his expression is severe, burdened by knowledge, and his aura is a chilling purity that closes wounds and stills pain yet carries the weight of irreversible judgment, marking him as the god who can restore life, but never innocence.
low_gods.lore: Dian Cecht-No-Chiyu represents the double-edged nature of healing: the power to save and the temptation to play god. His well of Slaine can restore the dead to life, but only if they are placed in it before their souls depart. He saved the Tuatha Dé Danann after the First Battle of Moytura, resurrecting slain warriors by singing over them in the well's waters. But his tragic flaw—professional jealousy—led him to kill his own son Miach, who had surpassed him by growing a new arm for Nuada where Dian Cecht could only make a silver replacement. This act created the first medical ethics: the healer's oath to prioritize the patient over pride.
low_gods.appearance: A stern, pale man with silver hair and cold blue eyes, wearing surgical robes over light armor. His hands are always clean and glowing with healing light.
low_gods.ascension_story: Was already a healing deity but achieved greater status by creating the Slaine Well—a feat that blurred the line between life and death so profoundly that it required divine oversight. His subsequent fall and redemption through teaching medical ethics completed his journey.

unique_abilities.name: Slaine Well Resurrection
unique_abilities.effect: Can restore the recently dead to life if their bodies are placed in his magical well within three days
unique_abilities.cooldown: The resurrected lose something essential (memories, emotions, or years of life)

unique_abilities.name: Fios Leighis (Medical Insight)
unique_abilities.effect: Can instantly diagnose any injury or illness, understanding its cause and optimal treatment
unique_abilities.cooldown: Continuous, but overwhelming with mass casualties

unique_abilities.name: Geis Leighis (Healer's Taboo)
unique_abilities.effect: Can place magical restrictions on healing that prevent certain conditions from being treated improperly
unique_abilities.cooldown: Each taboo requires a piece of his own vitality

low_gods.current_role: Chief physician of the Tuatha Dé Danann, guardian of medical ethics, teacher of healers.
duties: Maintaining the Slaine Well and regulating its use
Teaching healing arts and ethical boundaries
Treating gods wounded in divine conflicts
Judging medical malpractice cases
Preserving the balance between healing and natural death
sacred_items: The Slaine Well (resurrection waters)
Scalpel of Truth (cuts only what needs removing)
Mortar and Pestle of Balance (creates perfect medicinal mixtures)
Codex of Medical Ethics (writes itself with new cases)

rivals: His own guilt over his son's death
Deities of natural death who resent resurrection

weaknesses: Cannot heal himself of guilt or shame
Bound to treat any patient who reaches his well, regardless of their deeds
His healing powers fail when used out of pride or jealousy
Vulnerable to diseases of the spirit, not just the body

low_gods.name: Ogma-No-Moji, The Eloquent Strong
low_gods.god_of: God of eloquence and language who invented Ogham script. Also champion warrior.
low_gods.description: Ogma surges forward like a living siege engine, a colossal, armor-laden Celtic god with a powerful human face carved in confidence, dark skin gleaming beneath bronze plates inscribed with glowing Ogham, his mouth open mid-command as spoken words manifest as physical force, cracking stone and lifting armies; his immense club rests across his back like punctuation to violence, the background bending into vibrating glyphs and shattered battlements, while his aura is a thunderous pressure of persuasion and strength that proves language itself can be a weapon sharper than steel.
low_gods.lore: Ogma-No-Moji represents the unity of thought and action, of word and deed. He invented the Ogham alphabet not as mere symbols, but as containers of meaning that could alter reality when properly arranged. During the War of Words, when lies threatened to unravel reality itself, Ogma carved truth into the world-tree's bark, creating permanent anchors of meaning. As a warrior, he believes that strength without eloquence is brutality, and eloquence without strength is empty air. His most famous feat was single-handedly holding a mountain pass while simultaneously composing an epic poem about the battle, each stanza strengthening his allies and weakening his foes.
low_gods.appearance: A massive warrior with muscles like carved stone, covered in Ogham tattoos that glow when he speaks. Carries a club inscribed with his own poetry.
low_gods.ascension_story: Son of Dagda-No-Kyoten and the concept of 'meaningful action,' Ogma achieved divinity by creating a language so potent that speaking it could reshape small realities. His victory in the Contest of Champions—where he defeated seven enemies using only words that became weapons—secured his place among the high gods.

unique_abilities.name: Ogham Reality Scripting
unique_abilities.effect: Can carve Ogham runes that alter reality within their inscribed area, creating temporary laws or effects
unique_abilities.cooldown: Runes fade as their meaning is fulfilled or forgotten

unique_abilities.name: Briathar-Feidhm (Word-Function)
unique_abilities.effect: His spoken words manifest as physical forces—commands become binding, insults become wounds, praise becomes shields
unique_abilities.cooldown: Words must be truly meant and properly articulated

unique_abilities.name: Comhcheangal Teanga (Language Binding)
unique_abilities.effect: Can create temporary understanding between any beings, allowing communication regardless of language barriers
unique_abilities.cooldown: Lasts only as long as he maintains focus

low_gods.current_role: Keeper of Ogham script, champion-orator, patron of scholars and warriors.
duties: Preserving and teaching the Ogham alphabet
Serving as champion in disputes settled by words and deeds
Recording divine histories in permanent form
Teaching the martial applications of language
Judging contests of both poetry and strength
sacred_items: The Ogham Staves (carved wood that holds specific meanings)
Club of Eloquence (strikes with the weight of arguments)
Tongue of Truth (a literal tongue that can speak any language)
Stone Tablets of First Words (contain the original meanings)
weaknesses: Cannot speak lies without losing his voice
Bound to answer any properly formulated riddle or challenge
His strength wanes when his words are misunderstood
Vulnerable to perfect silence

low_gods.name: Epona-No-Ba, The Horse Mother
low_gods.god_of: Only Celtic goddess adopted by Romans. Protector of horses, riders, and stables.
low_gods.description: Epona rides straight out of myth into motion, a breathtaking Celtic goddess with radiant human beauty, warm ivory skin, thick thighs and a slender waist framed by minimal noble riding silks and gold tack-jewelry, her hair streaming as one with her magnificent steed whose hooves strike sparks of starlight; her posture is effortless dominance, her gaze protective yet alluring, and the background becomes an endless rolling plain stitched with spirit-roads, while her aura is a powerful, reassuring rhythm of trust, speed, and companionship that binds rider and mount into a single sacred force.
low_gods.lore: Epona-No-Ba emerged from the first partnership between human and horse, when a mortal girl calmed a wild stallion not through domination but through mutual understanding. She represents the bond that transforms animal and rider into a single being greater than the sum of its parts. Her protection extends to all who travel with goodwill, and her fertility blessings ensure that herds thrive and journeys bear fruit. When the Great Stampede threatened to destroy Skydrift's floating meadows, Epona rode at the head of the herd, turning their panic into a graceful dance that created new migratory patterns still followed today.
low_gods.appearance: A beautiful woman often depicted riding side-saddle on a magnificent white horse, wearing practical riding clothes adorned with horse brasses and bells.
low_gods.ascension_story: Began as a mortal horse-tamer whose bond with her mount was so profound that when she died, the collective grief of every horse in Skydrift echoed through the heavens. The Tuatha Dé Danann resurrected her as a goddess to honor the human-animal bond.

unique_abilities.name: Anam Capall (Horse-Soul Bond)
unique_abilities.effect: Can create perfect understanding between any rider and mount, making them move as one being
unique_abilities.cooldown: The bond lasts as long as mutual respect is maintained

unique_abilities.name: Bealach Sábháilte (Safe Passage)
unique_abilities.effect: Can bless roads and paths so that travelers following them avoid natural hazards and hostile encounters
unique_abilities.cooldown: One blessing per road, must be renewed annually

unique_abilities.name: Torthúlacht Tréad (Herd Fertility)
unique_abilities.effect: Can ensure the health and fertility of domesticated animals, particularly horses, within her blessed areas
unique_abilities.cooldown: Requires proper animal husbandry to maintain

low_gods.current_role: Protector of travelers, patron of horse breeding, guardian of roads and stables.
duties: Blessing new foals and riding partnerships
Protecting travelers on perilous journeys
Maintaining the spirit-roads between floating islands
Teaching proper animal husbandry
Settling disputes between nomadic and settled peoples
sacred_items: The Golden Bridle (fits any mount perfectly)
Horseshoes of Safe Travel (never wear out and prevent falls)
Mare's Milk Chalice (grants understanding of animal speech)
Saddle of Unity (makes rider and mount inseparable)

rivals: Deities of stagnation who oppose travel

weaknesses: Cannot refuse aid to a mistreated horse
Bound to protect any traveler who sincerely calls her name on the road
Her power wanes in completely settled, non-traveling communities
Vulnerable to betrayals of trust between rider and mount

low_gods.name: Sucellus-No-Tsuchi, The Good Striker
low_gods.god_of: God with large hammer (strikes earth for fertility) and pot (of eternal drink). Protector of farmers.
low_gods.description: Sucellus advances with seismic certainty, a massive, armor-clad Celtic god with deep earthen skin and a bearded human face etched in patience, his long-handled hammer descending mid-swing as the ground fractures into fertile fields and forests behind him; his armor is layered bark-metal and oak motifs, his stance immovable, and his aura is a heavy, comforting pulse of soil, ale, and seasonal certainty that reassures mortals that life will always return, no matter how hard the winter.
low_gods.lore: Sucellus-No-Tsuchi represents the patient, pounding work of agriculture and the rewards that follow. His hammer doesn't destroy—it awakens. Each strike on the earth releases dormant fertility, but only when struck with proper timing and respect. His pot of eternal drink represents the community that forms around shared labor and shared reward. During the Year of Barren Soil when crops failed across Skydrift, Sucellus taught mortals crop rotation and sustainable forestry, proving that true abundance comes from working with nature's rhythms, not against them.
low_gods.appearance: A burly, bearded man with earth-stained hands, carrying a large hammer over one shoulder and a drinking pot in the other hand. Wears simple farmer's clothes with armored pauldrons.
low_gods.ascension_story: Began as a mortal farmer whose fields always yielded triple their expected harvest. When he died, the land itself mourned, and his spirit merged with the soil he tended. Dagda-No-Kyoten recognized this as a new form of divinity—not rulership over nature, but partnership with it—and elevated him to godhood.

unique_abilities.name: Talamh Bheo (Living Earth Strike)
unique_abilities.effect: Striking the ground with his hammer awakens dormant fertility, causing crops to grow rapidly and abundantly
unique_abilities.cooldown: Each strike requires a season of rest for the land afterward

unique_abilities.name: Pota Síoraí (Eternal Pot)
unique_abilities.effect: His drinking pot never empties of nourishing liquid (usually ale or mead) and grants strength and camaraderie to those who share it
unique_abilities.cooldown: Only works when shared communally

unique_abilities.name: Dlí na nDúl (Law of the Elements)
unique_abilities.effect: Can enforce natural agricultural cycles, preventing unnatural growing seasons or exploitative harvesting
unique_abilities.cooldown: Only during seasonal transitions

low_gods.current_role: Patron of farmers and foresters, protector of agricultural communities, keeper of seasonal cycles.
duties: Blessing planting and harvest seasons
Teaching sustainable agriculture and forestry
Protecting farming communities from exploitation
Maintaining the quality of soil across floating islands
Preserving traditional brewing and fermentation knowledge
sacred_items: The Earth-Hammer (awakens fertility)
Eternal Drinking Pot
Seed-Bag of Plenty (produces appropriate seeds for any soil)
Farmer's Almanac (writes itself with optimal planting times)

rivals: Those who clear-cut forests without replanting

weaknesses: Cannot strike the earth in anger or greed
Bound to help any community facing famine
His hammer grows too heavy to lift during times of agricultural surplus wasted
Vulnerable to the corrosion of monoculture

low_gods.name: Taranis-No-Raimei, The Thunder Wheel
low_gods.god_of: God represented by wheel (sun/sky) and thunder. Human sacrifices burned in wicker man for him.
low_gods.description: Taranis descends within a spiraling storm, a towering Celtic god clad in radiant sky-forged armor, his muscular human frame crackling with lightning as he spins the blazing solar wheel like a cosmic weapon; his face is stern and luminous, eyes glowing with thunder's judgment, and the background fractures into storm-cloud temples and burning effigies of purification, while his aura is a deafening, electrified presence that annihilates corruption and shields the faithful, declaring him the terrifying mercy of the heavens made manifest.
low_gods.lore: Taranis-No-Raimei represents the necessary destruction that precedes renewal. His thunder isn't mindless violence—it's the sky's voice speaking truth to power. The wheel symbolizes both the sun's journey and the cycles of creation and destruction. The wicker man sacrifices of legend were actually symbolic: offerings of what needed to be purged from society (greed, corruption, stagnation), burned away so new growth could emerge. When the Corruption of Silent Skies threatened to make weather patterns stagnant and predictable, Taranis unleashed a storm that reshaped atmospheric currents, restoring necessary chaos to the system.
low_gods.appearance: A stern, majestic figure with hair of storm clouds and eyes that flash with lightning, holding a spinning wheel that glows like the sun. Armor made of thunderclouds and sunlight.
low_gods.ascension_story: Born from the first lightning strike that connected sky to earth, Taranis achieved full divinity during the Cleansing Storm, when he voluntarily contained a corruption so profound that it required burning away part of his own essence. His survival and regeneration proved that destruction in service of purity is a sacred act.

unique_abilities.name: Roth Gréine (Solar Wheel)
unique_abilities.effect: His spinning wheel can purify corruption, burn away spiritual pollution, and reveal hidden truths through illuminating light
unique_abilities.cooldown: Can only be spun during daylight or thunderstorms

unique_abilities.name: Toirneach Breithiúnais (Judgment Thunder)
unique_abilities.effect: His thunderbolts strike at injustice and corruption, destroying false structures and revealing underlying truths
unique_abilities.cooldown: Only strikes what truly deserves destruction

unique_abilities.name: Fear Bréige (Wicker Man Ritual)
unique_abilities.effect: Can create symbolic effigies that burn away societal ills when properly filled with representative offerings
unique_abilities.cooldown: Only during major seasonal transitions

low_gods.current_role: Purifier of corruption, bringer of necessary destruction, protector against spiritual decay.
duties: Cleansing areas of accumulated spiritual corruption
Judging cases of profound societal injustice
Maintaining the balance between stability and necessary change
Protecting the faithful from supernatural corruption
Overseeing purification rituals
sacred_items: The Solar Wheel (purification device)
Hammer of Thunder (summons lightning)
Wicker Man Frame (for ritual burnings)
Sky-Chariot (rides storm clouds)
weaknesses: Cannot destroy what is purely innocent
Bound to purify any corruption revealed to him
His thunder grows silent in completely stagnant, unchanging environments
Vulnerable to appeals for mercy when destruction is truly warranted

low_gods.name: Belanus-No-Hi, The Shining One
low_gods.god_of: Solar god associated with healing springs and fire. His festivals involve bonfires.
low_gods.description: Belanus strides from a veil of steam and sunlight, a noble, broad-chested Celtic god with glowing golden skin and serene human features, clad in radiant armor polished like dawn, a solar spear-staff in hand that emits healing light with every step; sacred springs erupt behind him into floating halos of mist and flame, and his aura is a piercing warmth that burns away disease and despair alike, revealing him as the benevolent yet uncompromising triumph of light over decay.
low_gods.lore: Belanus-No-Hi represents the sun not as a distant star, but as a healing presence. His light doesn't just illuminate—it purifies. His hot springs are where heaven's fire meets earth's water, creating places of healing and revelation. During the Plague of Shadows, when a darkness that physical light couldn't penetrate spread across Skydrift, Belanus discovered that his light could heal the spiritual decay that allowed the plague to thrive. His bonfire festivals aren't just celebrations—they're communal acts of purification, burning away the year's accumulated shadows to make room for new growth.
low_gods.appearance: A radiant man with skin like polished gold, hair like sunlight, and eyes that glow with gentle heat. Often shown emerging from steam or standing by sacred springs.
low_gods.ascension_story: Began as a mortal healer who discovered the first hot spring's curative properties. When he died, the spring dried up, only to return when his grateful patients prayed at its site. Their collective faith, combined with the spring's miraculous return, elevated him to divinity as the god of healing light.

unique_abilities.name: Solas Leighis (Healing Light)
unique_abilities.effect: His sunlight can cure diseases, heal wounds, and purify infections, both physical and spiritual
unique_abilities.cooldown: Most effective at noon; weakens at night

unique_abilities.name: Tobair Bheannaithe (Blessed Springs)
unique_abilities.effect: Can create or bless hot springs with healing properties that cure specific ailments for those who bathe in them
unique_abilities.cooldown: Each spring requires regular worship to maintain potency

unique_abilities.name: Tine Bealtaine (Beltane Fire)
unique_abilities.effect: Bonfires lit in his honor during festivals create zones of purification and fertility that last until the next festival
unique_abilities.cooldown: Only during specific solar festivals

low_gods.current_role: Healer through light and water, patron of hot springs, keeper of solar festivals.
duties: Maintaining the healing properties of sacred hot springs
Teaching solar-based healing techniques
Overseeing Beltane and other fire festivals
Protecting against diseases of darkness and despair
Guiding the sun's beneficial rays to needed areas
sacred_items: Solar Spear-Staff (channels healing sunlight)
Cauldron of Sacred Water (creates healing springs)
Bonfire Ember (never goes out and purifies what it burns)
Dawn Mirror (reflects healing light to inaccessible places)

rivals: Those who would pollute healing waters

weaknesses: Powerless in complete darkness
Cannot heal what refuses the light
Bound to answer any sincere request for healing at a sacred spring
His light dims when healing is commodified rather than gifted

low_gods.name: Macha-No-Kyoso, The Horse Race
low_gods.god_of: Goddess who outran king's horses while pregnant. Protector of land and its fertility.
low_gods.description: Macha appears as a pregnant woman running with impossible speed, her human form both vulnerable and terrifyingly powerful, sweat and earth mingling on her sun-bronzed skin as she outraces the wind itself, her rounded belly not a burden but the sacred center of her momentum; behind her, the land itself reshapes, hills flattening into plains for her passage, rivers changing course to follow, and the very sky streaks with the colors of sunset caught in her hair, while her aura is the fierce, protective pulse of a mother defending her home, declaring that fertility is not passive but a force that can outrun any threat.
low_gods.lore: Macha-No-Kyoso embodies the protective, fierce aspect of fertility. When the king of Ulster forced her, while nine months pregnant, to race against his horses, she won but cursed his kingdom with the weakness of labor pains during times of crisis. This wasn't vengeance but a lesson: the land's fertility and the people's strength are interconnected, and to exploit one is to weaken both. She represents sovereignty as something earned through respect for the land, not domination over it. Her curses are actually teachings in painful form.
low_gods.appearance: A powerfully built pregnant woman with wild hair, often shown running with superhuman speed. Her eyes hold both maternal warmth and warrior's fury.
low_gods.ascension_story: Began as a mortal woman of the Tuatha Dé Danann who married a Ulster king. Her humiliation and subsequent curse were so profound that they altered the land's relationship with its rulers permanently. This act of geis-creation through personal sacrifice elevated her to divinity.

unique_abilities.name: Rás an Talaimh (Race of the Land)
unique_abilities.effect: Can run faster than any natural creature while pregnant, and her passage temporarily enhances the fertility of the land she crosses
unique_abilities.cooldown: Only while carrying life within her

unique_abilities.name: Geis Ulaidh (Ulster's Curse)
unique_abilities.effect: Can place a curse on rulers or kingdoms that causes them to experience the weakness of childbirth during crises if they disrespect fertility
unique_abilities.cooldown: The curse lasts nine generations or until proper restitution is made

unique_abilities.name: Talamh Cosanta (Land's Protection)
unique_abilities.effect: Can awaken the land itself to defend against invaders, causing terrain to shift and natural hazards to appear
unique_abilities.cooldown: Only when the land is truly threatened

low_gods.current_role: Protector of pregnant women, enforcer of land-sovereignty bonds, patron of warrior-mothers.
duties: Protecting pregnant women from exploitation
Enforcing the sacred bond between rulers and their land
Teaching that fertility requires protection, not just celebration
Judging disputes between agricultural and warrior classes
Maintaining the balance between human needs and land's health
sacred_items: The Running Sash (grants supernatural speed to pregnant wearers)
Plow-Sword (tills earth or defends it equally well)
Womb-Stone (protects unborn children)
Crown of Earth (only fits rulers who respect their land)

rivals: Those who would separate sovereignty from land stewardship
protected: Communities that live in balance with their environment
Warriors who fight to protect their homes

weaknesses: Cannot refuse a challenge to race while pregnant
Bound to protect any pregnant woman in danger
Her power wanes in lands where the ruler-soil bond is completely broken
Vulnerable to appeals that separate protection from control

demi_gods.name: Draoi-Fionn
demi_gods.title: The Oak-Speaker
demi_gods.description: Draoi-Fionn rises from the heart of the Floating Groves like a living embodiment of ancient forests, his bark-hued skin engraved with glowing runes, muscles sculpted like carved oak, and eyes swirling with deep emerald wisdom, reflecting centuries of tree consciousness. Leaves, moss, and miniature branches grow from his flowing hair, twisting with faint whispers of forgotten groves, while his gnarled Whispering Staff hums with the voices of every tree, sprouting spectral branches mid-air. He wears living vine robes that curl and move like sentient serpents, adorned with bronze oak talismans, and a belt of tiny, floating saplings. Draoi-Fionn’s posture is commanding yet fluid, arms outstretched as if conversing with the world itself, a gilded aura of green and gold pulsing around him, sending drifting seeds and ethereal pollen into the sky. Behind him, a grove of massive, floating trees rises impossibly into the clouds, their branches bending toward him as if bowing. He negotiated cures for blights that threatened his realm and united the groves’ consciousness, earning the essence of the First Oak from Cernunnos-No-Shizen and cementing his place as the Oak-Speaker, a demi-god whose voice is the heartbeat of forests.
demi_gods.lore: Born as a humble druid in Skydrift’s highest floating grove, Fionn spent seven years in complete silence, listening to the whispers of every tree until their ancient languages became his own. When a blight threatened the floating forests, he negotiated with each species, learning their immunities and secrets, and forged a cure that saved the groves from destruction. Witnessing his communion with nature, Cernunnos-No-Shizen infused him with the essence of the First Oak, granting him demi-godhood as the Oak-Speaker, the voice of the forests. Now, Fionn can communicate with any plant through Comhrá Crann, draw multiple plants into a unified consciousness with Grove-Mind, and mediate between flora and mortals alike, teaching respect for all life. His deeds echo through the branches of every tree, and his bark-like skin, leafy hair, and aura of green-gold mark him as the eternal guardian of the Floating Groves.
demi_gods.full_title: Druid Who Learned The Language Of Every Tree In The Floating Groves
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Druid from the highest floating grove in Skydrift
demi_gods.ascension_story: Fionn spent seven years in silence, listening to the trees until he understood each species' unique language. When a blight threatened to destroy the floating groves, he negotiated with the trees to share their ancient immunities, creating a cure that saved the entire ecosystem. Cernunnos-No-Shizen, impressed by this respectful communication, infused him with the essence of the First Oak, granting him demi-divinity as the voice of the groves.
demi_gods.appearance: A man with bark-like skin, leaves growing from his hair, and eyes that show shifting forest patterns. His voice carries the sound of wind through leaves. Wears simple druidic robes woven from living vines.

unique_abilities.name: Comhrá Crann
unique_abilities.effect: Can communicate with any plant life, understanding their memories, needs, and wisdom
unique_abilities.limitations: Plants must be willing to communicate; cannot force them to speak

unique_abilities.name: Grove-Mind
unique_abilities.effect: Can temporarily connect multiple plants into a shared consciousness for problem-solving or defense
unique_abilities.limitations: Requires physical connection between plants; broken if the connection is severed

demi_gods.current_role: Chief interpreter for the Floating Groves and teacher of tree languages
duties: Mediates between plant life and other beings
Teaches druids respectful communication with flora
Maintains the Library of Tree Songs
Advises on ecological balance in floating islands
sacred_items: The Whispering Staff (amplifies plant voices)
Acorn of Tongues (when planted, allows temporary understanding of plant language)
temples: The Speaking Grove (a circle of ancient trees that answer questions)
Root-chambers in major floating islands

rivals: Entities that spread plant diseases intentionally
students: A circle of 13 druids learning tree languages

weaknesses: Cannot communicate with completely artificial plants
Weakened in areas devoid of plant life
Compelled to translate for any plant that requests communication

demi_gods.name: Sidhe-Caoimhe
demi_gods.title: The Mound's Grace
demi_gods.description: Sidhe-Caoimhe hovers above the neutral mounds like a seductive, ethereal queen, silver skin radiant with moonlight, wings of crystal-shadow beating softly as starlight refracts through them. Her curves, thin waist, and powerful thighs are wrapped in minimal, shifting robes of gossamer silk that flicker between mortal wool and fairy threads, embroidered with glowing Celtic runes. In one hand, she holds the Threshold Stone, etched with protective sigils, while the Balanced Cup floats by her side, radiating a gentle, lilac light. Her eyes, deep pools reflecting both mortal and fairy realms, command attention and inspire trust, while her presence exudes an aura of silver, violet, and spectral motes, bending magic and perception around her. Around her, the background shifts—a dense forest and a shimmering fairy glade blending seamlessly, suggesting her dual mastery over realms. She sacrificed immortality to protect mortals and negotiate peace, earning Brigid-No-Shono’s blessing as a demi-goddess. Her dynamic posture, poised mid-flight with wings unfurled, signals both grace and deadly authority: the Mound’s Grace, a guardian of cross-realm mercy.
demi_gods.lore: Caoimhe, a noble fairy of the Sidhe courts, fell in love with a mortal and, in defending his village, challenged the cruel whims of her own people, teaching them to respect humans. When the court threatened to erase the village, she sacrificed her immortality to erect a permanent protective ward. Moved by her selflessness, Brigid-No-Shono restored her as a demi-goddess, granting her dominion over fairy-human relations and earning the title the Mound’s Grace. Her abilities include piercing fairy illusions with Géar-Éadrom and creating protective boundaries through Teorainn Cosanta, and she now serves as ambassador between realms, guiding mortals and fairies toward respectful coexistence. Her ethereal silver glow, crystal-shadow wings, and shifting robes mark her as a figure of beauty, mercy, and irresistible authority, bridging two worlds.
demi_gods.full_title: Fairy Queen Who Protected Mortals From Her Own Kind
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Sidhe (fairy) noble who fell in love with a mortal
demi_gods.ascension_story: Caoimhe defended her mortal lover's village from fairy tricks and kidnappings, teaching her people to respect mortals rather than toy with them. When her own court threatened to erase the village from memory, she sacrificed her fairy immortality to create a permanent protection ward. Brigid-No-Shono, goddess of threefold arts, was moved by this selfless love and restored her as a demi-goddess, making her the guardian of balanced fairy-mortal relations.
demi_gods.appearance: A being of ethereal beauty with faint silver glow, wings of crystal and shadow, and eyes that show both fairy realms and mortal world. Wears garments that shift between fairy silks and mortal wool.

unique_abilities.name: Géar-Éadrom
unique_abilities.effect: Can see through fairy glamour and reveal true intentions, showing both the beautiful and dangerous truths
unique_abilities.limitations: Cannot create or maintain glamour herself anymore

unique_abilities.name: Teorainn Cosanta
unique_abilities.effect: Can create boundaries that protect mortals from harmful fairy magic while allowing beneficial interactions
unique_abilities.limitations: Boundaries require consent from both sides to establish

demi_gods.current_role: Ambassador between Sidhe courts and mortal settlements
duties: Negotiates fairy-mortal treaties
Rescues mortals from harmful fairy attention
Teaches both sides respectful interaction
Maintains the Neutral Mounds where both can meet safely
sacred_items: The Balanced Cup (when drunk from, reveals one's true nature to both fairy and mortal sight)
Threshold Stone (marks a permanently neutral boundary)
temples: The Mound of Meeting (a hill that exists in both realms simultaneously)
Waystations at fairy paths

allies: Alf-Hjarta (from Wildheart, fellow cross-realm relationship deity)
rivals: Malicious fairies who prey on mortals
Mortal fairy-hunters who harm innocent fey
family: Her mortal husband and their half-fairy children

weaknesses: Cannot take sides in fairy-mortal conflicts
Powerless against those who completely reject either nature
Compelled to mediate any fairy-mortal dispute brought to her

demi_gods.name: Bard-Ortha
demi_gods.title: The Oath-Singer
demi_gods.description: Bard-Ortha commands the floating amphitheater like a celestial maestro, his muscular, broad frame swathed in flowing robes etched with runes that shimmer with musical energy, and a glowing golden harp embedded in his chest, strings vibrating in tandem with his heartbeat. His eyes shimmer with living musical notation, hair dancing subtly to unseen melodies, and a luminous quill hovers, writing contracts in the air that emit faint silver sparks. Every motion radiates an aura of blue, gold, and violet, warping reality subtly as his songs bind promises and enforce truth. Behind him, the sky tears open to reveal a swirling vortex of musical symbols and treaties, reflecting the power of his binding songs across kingdoms. His dynamic posture—one arm extended to raise a note into reality while the other guides a glowing, floating scroll—projects authority, artistry, and divine presence. By ending wars, compelling truth, and creating unbreakable treaties, he earned Lugh-No-Sainou’s demi-god blessing, becoming the Oath-Singer whose music shapes reality itself.
demi_gods.lore: A court bard with uncanny musical talent, Ortha discovered that promises made under his songs became magically binding. Using this power, he forged unbreakable treaties, ended wars, and compelled truth in justice proceedings. Recognized by Lugh-No-Sainou for his artistry and innovation, he was elevated to demi-godhood as the Oath-Singer, patron of binding arts. Ortha wields Geasa-Ceol to craft magical geasa through music and Focal-Fírinne to enforce truth, ensuring promises cannot be broken. His harp-heart, glowing quill, and musical aura of blue, gold, and violet bend reality to harmony, allowing him to mediate disputes, maintain archives of sung promises, and teach the next generation of bards, forever linking music, law, and magic.
demi_gods.full_title: Bard Whose Songs Made Promises Binding On Reality
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Court bard who discovered his songs could magically bind listeners
demi_gods.ascension_story: Ortha's performances were so compelling that promises made during his songs became magically binding. He used this power to end wars by making treaties unbreakable and to ensure justice by binding witnesses to truth. Lugh-No-Sainou, god of all arts, recognized this as a new form of artistic mastery and granted him demi-divinity as the patron of binding arts.
demi_gods.appearance: A man with a harp for a heart, vocal cords that glow when he sings, and eyes that show musical notation. His hair moves as if to silent music. Writes constantly in the air with a glowing quill.

unique_abilities.name: Geasa-Ceol
unique_abilities.effect: His songs can create magical geasa (taboos/bindings) that are extremely difficult to break without consequences
unique_abilities.limitations: The bound must consent to the song's theme; cannot create arbitrary restrictions

unique_abilities.name: Focal-Fírinne
unique_abilities.effect: Can compel truth in speech when playing, making lies physically painful to utter
unique_abilities.limitations: Only works within earshot of his music; listeners can choose silence

demi_gods.current_role: Chief negotiator and treaty-singer for Skydrift's floating kingdoms
duties: Sings binding treaties between nations
Teaches bards responsible use of binding magic
Maintains the Archive of Sung Promises
Adjudicates disputes over broken musical oaths
sacred_items: The Harp of Binding (its strings vibrate when promises are broken)
Quill of Final Words (writes contracts that cannot be misinterpreted)
temples: The Hall of Echoing Promises
Amphitheaters used for treaty-signings

rivals: Deities of chaos and broken words
apprentices: Seven bardic students learning binding songs

weaknesses: Cannot break his own word or songs
Powerless against the completely tone-deaf
Compelled to sing binding for any treaty requested by both parties in good faith

demi_gods.name: Fianna-Scáth
demi_gods.title: The Shadow-Hunter
demi_gods.description: Fianna-Scáth emerges from the void like a predatory god of shadow, his muscular, human-form body half-swallowed in darkness, ebony skin absorbing light, eyes glowing silver to pierce the void, veins subtly etched with luminescent runes. Dark leather armor, embossed with Celtic patterns and void-glyphs, hugs his frame while his Void-Blade and Shadow-Cloak writhe like living shadows, pulsing with obsidian-blue energy that distorts light and reality around him. He crouches on the edge of a floating island, tendrils of shadow stretching behind him into infinite non-space, a posture ready to spring into any void crack. His aura is a living night, deep black and blue, with spectral silhouettes of void-beasts swirling around, as if paying homage. By hunting the darkness threatening floating islands and navigating impossible voids, he gained Morrigan-No-Yogen’s blessing, becoming the Shadow-Hunter, a demi-god sentinel of the interstitial spaces, terrifying and heroic, bridging the mortal and the void realms.
demi_gods.lore: A hunter from the islands on the brink of the void, Scáth trained to pursue creatures that slipped between realms, mastering navigation through shadow and non-space. When a void-beast threatened to annihilate an island, he pursued it through impossible darkness, defeating it in a realm without light. Morrigan-No-Yogen recognized his courage and skill, bestowing him demi-god status as the Shadow-Hunter, guardian of the spaces between floating islands. Scáth wields Dorchadas-Taisteal to travel through shadows and Scáth-Maraithe to strike void entities immune to normal weapons. His half-shadow form, void-absorbing skin, obsidian-blue armor, and glowing eyes allow him to patrol the boundaries between worlds, keeping darkness at bay and training others in the art of void hunting.
demi_gods.full_title: Warrior Who Hunted The Darkness Between Floating Islands
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Hunter from a tribe that lived on islands closest to the void between worlds
demi_gods.ascension_story: Scáth specialized in hunting creatures that slipped through the shadows between floating islands. When a void-beast threatened to consume an entire island, he tracked it through impossible non-space and defeated it in a realm without light. Morrigan-No-Yogen, goddess of fate and war, was impressed by this fearless navigation and granted him demi-divinity as the guardian of the spaces between.
demi_gods.appearance: A man who seems half-made of shadow, with eyes that see in absolute darkness, and skin that drinks light. Carries weapons that cut through void-substance. Moves silently between patches of darkness.

unique_abilities.name: Dorchadas-Taisteal
unique_abilities.effect: Can travel through shadows and voids between places, appearing from any dark spot
unique_abilities.limitations: Requires darkness at both origin and destination; cannot travel through complete light

unique_abilities.name: Scáth-Maraithe
unique_abilities.effect: Can harm beings made of shadow, void, or negative space that are immune to normal weapons
unique_abilities.limitations: Only effective against non-corporeal or void-based beings

demi_gods.current_role: Protector of island boundaries and hunter of void-creatures
duties: Patrols the spaces between floating islands
Hunts creatures that threaten from the void
Teaches navigation through shadow-paths
Maintains warning systems for void incursions
sacred_items: The Void-Blade (cuts through non-substance)
Shadow-Cloak (allows movement through darkness)
temples: The Edge Keep (built on an island facing the void)
Shadow-sanctuaries in places of permanent darkness

rivals: Those who would open gates to dangerous voids

weaknesses: Weakened in bright, shadowless light
Cannot enter areas of pure, magical light
Compelled to investigate any reported void-incursion
demi_gods.symbol: Eye staring from within a shadow

demi_gods.name: Craobh-Síol
demi_gods.title: The Seed of the World Tree
demi_gods.description: Craobh-Síol radiates life-force and creation, her fertile skin shimmering with moss and flower petals, hair like twisting roots adorned with blossoms and tiny, glowing insects. Minimal, rune-etched robes cling to her seductive form, highlighting her thin waist and powerful thighs, while she cradles the Growth-Harp, whose music causes plants to sprout instantly, and the Seed-Pouch, glowing with floating seeds ready to create new islands. Her aura pulses gold and green, scattering miniature ecosystems and motes of magic around her, while behind her, an entire new floating island rises from a luminous acorn, glowing and alive, water and vegetation forming in real time. Mid-motion, arms raised, her posture conveys the godly act of Oileán-Cruthú, the birth of life and new worlds. By singing seven years to stabilize and grow a new landmass, she earned Dagda-No-Kyoten’s blessing, becoming the Seed of the World Tree, a goddess whose very breath creates islands and life.
demi_gods.lore: A druid tending a small, struggling floating island, Síol nurtured it with careful cultivation until it threatened to sink. She planted a sacred acorn at its heart and sang continuous growth-songs for seven years, stabilizing and expanding the island into a thriving ecosystem. Dagda-No-Kyoten witnessed her feat and granted her demi-godhood as the Seed of the World Tree, mother of new floating lands. She wields Oileán-Cruthú to grow islands from blessed seeds and Aer-Fhás to cultivate plants in aerial environments, maintaining the balance of Skydrift’s floating ecosystems. Her soil-toned skin, root-like hair, and aura of life mark her as the ultimate nurturer of creation, spreading life, teaching aerial agriculture, and creating refuge islands wherever needed.
demi_gods.full_title: Druid Who Grew A New Floating Island From A Single Acorn
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Druid who tended the smallest floating island in Skydrift
demi_gods.ascension_story: Síol cultivated her tiny island until it could support an entire ecosystem. When it began to sink, she planted a sacred acorn at its heart and sang growth-songs for seven years without stopping. The island not only stabilized but grew tenfold, becoming a new major floating landmass. Dagda-No-Kyoten, the Good God of abundance, witnessed this creation and granted her demi-divinity as the mother of new islands.
demi_gods.appearance: A woman with soil for skin that grows moss and small flowers, hair like flowing roots, and hands that constantly scatter seeds. Her breath smells of fertile earth and rain.

unique_abilities.name: Oileán-Cruthú
unique_abilities.effect: Can cause new floating islands to grow from specially blessed seeds, complete with stable ecosystems
unique_abilities.limitations: Growth takes years; requires continuous care and singing

unique_abilities.name: Aer-Fhás
unique_abilities.effect: Can make plants grow in aerial environments without soil, using magic and mist
unique_abilities.limitations: Plants are magically sustained and require her ongoing attention or a druid's care

demi_gods.current_role: Creator and tender of new floating islands
duties: Grows new islands for overcrowded populations
Teaches aerial agriculture techniques
Maintains the balance of Skydrift's floating ecosystem
Preserves rare plant species on specially grown sanctuary islands
sacred_items: The Seed-Pouch (produces appropriate seeds for any environment)
Growth-Harp (its music accelerates plant growth)
temples: The Nursery Island (her first and greatest creation)
Germination chambers on various islands

rivals: Those who destroy islands for resources
creations: Dozens of floating islands she has grown

weaknesses: Cannot harm any plant life, even to save herself
Powerless in completely sterile environments
Compelled to help any island ecosystem in danger of collapse
demi_gods.symbol: Acorn with roots forming an island

demi_gods.name: Bean-Sídhe-Trua
demi_gods.title: The Mourning Singer
demi_gods.description: Bean-Sídhe-Trua floats like a sorrowful goddess of death, silver-tinged skin radiant with ethereal light, hair cascading like mourning veils interwoven with spectral tears, her thin waist and curvaceous thighs wrapped in flowing, translucent robes that swirl with every gust of wind. Her eyes, reflecting endless deaths, pierce mortal and fairy hearts alike, while the Tear-Vial and Veil of Sorrows glow softly, capturing memories and easing departures. She hovers above an otherworldly landscape where ghostly souls drift, her posture dynamic—arms outstretched in lament, aura of deep violet, silver, and faint gold radiating divine compassion. Every motion weaves Caoineadh-Uile and Cuimhne-Glacadh, turning grief into peace and preserving memories across realms. By weeping for strangers and allies alike, she broke banshee taboos, earning Morrigan-No-Yogen’s blessing, becoming the Mourning Singer, a seductive, ethereal demi-goddess whose song ensures no life passes ungrieved, her presence a bittersweet fusion of beauty, sorrow, and divine mercy.
demi_gods.lore: Trua, a banshee from a minor noble family, defied banshee tradition by mourning not only her kin but strangers, enemies, and the forgotten, using her voice to ease every passing. When she wept for a dying enemy, breaking ancient taboos, Morrigan-No-Yogen was moved and granted her demi-god status as the Mourning Singer, patron of compassionate death. Trua wields Caoineadh-Uile to soothe souls during transition and Cuimhne-Glacadh to preserve cherished memories, ensuring that no life passes ungrieved. Her silver tears, mourning-veil hair, and swirling robes radiate violet-silver-gold light, and her presence hovers over the dying like an ethereal embrace, turning sorrow into mercy, grief into divine memory, and ensuring that death itself carries both beauty and compassion.
demi_gods.full_title: Banshee Who Wept For Strangers As Well As Kin
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Banshee (fairy death-singer) from a minor noble family
demi_gods.ascension_story: Unlike other banshees who only sing for their own bloodline, Trua felt every death as personal loss. She would appear to sing for strangers, paupers, and even enemies, her voice carrying such compassion that it eased the passing. When she wept for a dying enemy of her family, breaking ancient banshee taboos, the Morrigan heard her song and was moved. Instead of punishing her, the goddess granted her demi-divinity as the patron of compassionate death.
demi_gods.appearance: A sorrowful yet beautiful woman with silver tears that turn to pearls, hair like mourning veils, and a voice that echoes with lost memories. Wears simple grey robes that flutter as if in perpetual wind.

unique_abilities.name: Caoineadh-Uile
unique_abilities.effect: Her lament can ease any soul's passing, regardless of their deeds or beliefs, ensuring peaceful transition
unique_abilities.limitations: Cannot prevent death, only ease it; requires her to genuinely feel the loss

unique_abilities.name: Cuimhne-Glacadh
unique_abilities.effect: Can preserve the most cherished memory of the dying, storing it in her tears to share with loved ones
unique_abilities.limitations: Only one memory per person; the memory fades from the dying as it's taken

demi_gods.current_role: Comforter of the dying and preserver of final memories
duties: Sings for those who would die unmourned
Collects and shares final memories
Teaches healthy grieving practices
Maintains the Hall of Remembered Souls
sacred_items: The Tear-Vial (stores memories in liquid form)
Veil of Sorrows (when worn, allows understanding of others' grief)
temples: The Quiet House (a place for peaceful dying)
Memory-gardens where her tears have fallen

rivals: Those who cause unnecessary suffering in death
Deities who see death only as punishment
comforted: Countless souls she has eased into death

weaknesses: Cannot refuse a sincere request for comforting at death
Powerless to help those who welcome death with joy
Carries the grief of all she comforts
demi_gods.symbol: Tear with a face reflected inside

sidhe_courts.description: The ruling families of the fairy realms (Aos Sí), each governing different aspects of the magical world. They are minor divinities of glamour, enchantment, and the subtle arts of illusion and nature magic.

hierarchy.role: Govern the seven major fairy realms in Skydrift

examples.name: Daoine-Uaine
examples.title: The Green Court
examples.appearance: Noble fairies with leaf-wing, bark-skin, and crowns of living flowers, surrounded by perpetual spring
duties: Maintain the magical forests of the floating islands
Control the growth cycles of enchanted plants
Teach respectful use of plant magic
Preserve ancient groves from corruption
examples.unique_power: Can cause any plant to grow, change, or bloom instantly, but only according to its natural potential

examples.name: Daoine-Gorm
examples.title: The Blue Court
examples.appearance: Ethereal fairies with water-skin, rain-hair, and wings of mist, voices like flowing streams
duties: Maintain the waterfalls and rains of floating islands
Create the rainbows that connect islands
Control mist and cloud formations
Teach the language of water and weather
examples.unique_power: Can create temporary bridges of rainbow light between islands, but only in proper sunlight after rain

hierarchy.role: Manage specialized aspects of fairy magic and territory

examples.name: Teaghlach-Ceol
examples.title: The Music Household
examples.appearance: Fairies with instrument-limb, sound-wave hair, and voices that harmonize perfectly
duties: Create the background music of fairy realms
Teach musical magic to bards
Maintain the natural harmonies of floating islands
Compose songs that influence growth and emotion

examples.name: Teaghlach-Samhail
examples.title: The Mirror Household
examples.appearance: Fairies with mirror-skin, glass-wing, and eyes that show reflections rather than pupils
duties: Maintain pools and surfaces that show truth
Create glamours that reveal rather than conceal
Teach how to see through deception
Protect against harmful illusions

hierarchy.role: Individual fairy folk with specific talents and domains

types.appearance: Beautiful, seductive fairies with rose-petal skin and honey-voice, surrounded by faint love-magic
types.typical_domain: Artists' studios, poets' groves, lovers' meeting places, creative spaces
types.organization: Often solitary or in small groups centered around specific artists or lovers

types.appearance: Charming, talkative fairies with silver-tongues and eyes that promise secrets, always well-dressed
types.typical_domain: Markets, taverns, negotiation chambers, social gatherings
types.organization: Network through social circles, forming information webs

types.appearance: Red-clad fairy gentlemen with impeccable manners, sharp features, and an air of dangerous courtesy
types.typical_domain: Roads, bridges, thresholds, places of meeting and parting
types.organization: Solitary guardians of specific locations or traditions

sidhe_courts.recruitment: Born as fairies or transformed from mortals through ancient pacts or powerful magic; can also be created by higher fairy nobility for specific purposes
sidhe_courts.mortality: Long-lived but not immortal; can be killed by iron, broken promises, or loss of all belief in them; fade if their specific magic becomes obsolete
sidhe_courts.worship: Receive offerings of milk, honey, shiny objects, artistic creations, and respectful attention; dislike direct worship but appreciate gifts and remembrance

fomorian_clans.description: Ancient, monstrous beings representing the wild, chaotic aspects of nature. Though often depicted as enemies in myths, they are necessary forces of change, challenge, and raw power in Skydrift's balance.

hierarchy.role: Powerful beings who challenge the established order and test the strength of civilizations

examples.name: Balor-Glas
examples.mortal_achievement: Ruled the floating islands before the coming of the gods, establishing the first laws of magic and conflict
examples.current_form: A massive giant with stone-grey skin, one eye that sees truth and one that sees possibility, carrying a club made of petrified lightning
examples.serves: As an independent force that tests gods and mortals alike
examples.unique_power: His gaze can temporarily strip away civilization's protections, revealing the raw nature beneath

examples.name: Bres-Fionn
examples.mortal_achievement: Ruled as both fairy king and mortal tyrant, understanding both natures perfectly
examples.current_form: A stunningly beautiful giant with perfect features but cold eyes, wearing armor of gold and thorns
examples.serves: As a warning against beauty without compassion and rule without wisdom
examples.unique_power: Can make anything or anyone temporarily perfect, but the perfection is cold and unsustainable

hierarchy.role: Enforcers and challengers who test the strength of heroes and civilizations

examples.name: Cichol-Cos-Gearr
examples.mortal_achievement: Fought in every major battle of the ancient times, never defeated despite his disability
examples.current_form: A massive warrior hopping on one powerful leg, using a spear as his second leg in battle
examples.serves: As the patron of those who overcome physical limitations to achieve greatness
examples.unique_power: Can temporarily grant incredible prowess to those with physical disadvantages, but only in defense of their homes

fomorian_clans.ascension_process: Born as Fomorians or transformed through exposure to primordial chaos magic; achieve status through great deeds of chaos, challenge, or rulership
fomorian_clans.limitations: Bound by ancient geasa (taboos) specific to each individual; often weakened by symbols of civilization and order
fomorian_clans.shrines: Rarely worshipped directly, but have monuments at sites of their great battles or rule; some outcast groups make offerings to them for protection or power

ulster_heroes.description: Mortal heroes of great renown who have achieved minor divinity through extraordinary deeds. They serve as inspirations, protectors, and sometimes warnings about the costs of heroism.

types.appearance: Warriors in battle-frenzy or warp-spasm, with distorted features and terrifying prowess, weapons glowing with battle-light
types.intelligence: Battle-consciousness (understand combat, honor, fury, and the line between hero and monster)
duties: Test other warriors in single combat
Defend sacred places through personal challenge
Teach the arts of focused combat
Serve as examples of both heroic glory and its costs
types.communication: Through combat challenges, battle cries, and dreams of glory to aspiring warriors

types.appearance: Steadfast warriors with shield-arm stronger than sword-arm, eyes that show loyalty, and presence that strengthens allies
types.intelligence: Companion-consciousness (understand friendship, loyalty, sacrifice, and group strength)
duties: Protect heroes and important figures
Teach the value of loyalty and fellowship
Maintain warrior codes and companionship traditions
Serve as the ideal of the true friend and ally
types.communication: Through gestures of solidarity, shared silence, and dreams of camaraderie

types.appearance: Noble warriors with sorrowful eyes, carrying weapons that remember every life taken, surrounded by faint ghostly echoes
types.intelligence: Tragic-consciousness (understand cost, consequence, regret, and the price of violence)
duties: Warn against glory without wisdom
Comfort those burdened by their deeds
Teach the true costs of war and heroism
Serve as reminders that every action has consequence
types.communication: Through sorrowful songs, cautionary tales, and dreams that show the aftermath of glory

ulster_heroes.creation: Achieve minor divinity through legendary deeds, tragic deaths, or overwhelming legacy; often elevated by gods, bards, or the collective memory of their people
ulster_heroes.lifespan: Immortal as long as their stories are told; fade if completely forgotten but can be revived by rediscovery of their tales
ulster_heroes.worship: Receive offerings at their burial sites, places of great deeds, and through recitation of their stories; warriors make offerings before battle for their favor

banshee_choirs.description: Spirit women who sing before deaths, particularly in old families. They are minor divinities of fate, warning, and the connection between life and death.

notable_embodiments.name: Bean-Chlann
notable_embodiments.appearance: A sorrowful woman in grey, with family resemblance to those she mourns, voice carrying generations of loss
notable_embodiments.manifestation_conditions: Appears before the death of a family member in old, magical bloodlines
notable_embodiments.power: Her song can prepare the dying and their family for the passing, easing the transition
notable_embodiments.limitation: Only appears for her specific family; cannot warn of or ease other deaths

notable_embodiments.name: Bean-Áite
notable_embodiments.appearance: A localized spirit tied to a specific location, appearing as a mist-woman with features of the land
notable_embodiments.manifestation_conditions: Appears before deaths that will occur in her specific location
notable_embodiments.power: Can warn those about to die in her place to make final preparations or leave if possible
notable_embodiments.limitation: Bound to her location; cannot warn of deaths elsewhere

notable_embodiments.name: Bean-Tuar
notable_embodiments.appearance: A prophetic spirit with future-sight eyes, singing of possibilities rather than certainties
notable_embodiments.manifestation_conditions: Appears when someone's actions could lead to their death, singing of possible outcomes
notable_embodiments.power: Her song can show possible death-scenarios, allowing the warned to change their path
notable_embodiments.limitation: Only shows possibilities, not certainties; cannot guarantee survival even if heeded

banshee_choirs.birth_process: Form when a woman dies with unfinished mourning or deep connection to family/place, or when created by death deities to serve specific families or locations
banshee_choirs.power_source: Draw strength from the grief they witness and the transitions they facilitate; grow stronger with each generation they serve
banshee_choirs.vulnerability: Weaken if their family dies out or their place is destroyed; fade if no one hears or heeds their warnings

druidic_circles.description: Organizations of druids who have achieved minor divinity through mastery of nature magic, wisdom, and service to balance. They maintain the sacred knowledge of Skydrift.

departments.head: Draoi-Fios, Chief of Vision
departments.staff: 13 master seers (one for each lunar month), 52 apprentice seers
duties: Maintain prophetic traditions and sites
Interpret omens and visions for the people
Keep the calendar of sacred times
Train new seers in responsible prophecy
departments.office_location: The Grove of Vision, where the trees show possible futures in their bark

departments.head: Breitheamh-Cothrom, Judge of Balance
departments.staff: 7 high judges, 49 regional judges, countless local arbiters
duties: Maintain and interpret druidic law
Adjudicate disputes according to natural justice
Preserve legal traditions and precedents
Train new judges in wisdom and fairness
departments.office_location: The Circle of Judgment, where the land itself witnesses proceedings

supreme_god.name: Olodumare-No-Hasshin, The Supreme Source
supreme_god.title: Owner of the Palace of Heaven
supreme_god.god_of: The distant, all-powerful creator who exists beyond the Shattered Expanse. Does not interact directly but emanates the Ashe (divine energy) that powers all things. The other gods are his aspects and messengers.
supreme_god.description: Olodumare-No-Hasshin manifests as the unfathomable source from which all Ashe flows, a being of paradox who exists simultaneously as infinite darkness and blinding light, as the silent void before creation and the deafening choir of all existence. His form shifts between an ancient elder whose skin holds the night sky with stars that birth and die in his pores, and a formless radiance that illuminates without revealing. When he chooses to manifest, he appears as an impossibly old yet ageless figure of indeterminate gender, draped in cloth woven from the first light and final darkness, sitting on a throne carved from the primordial silence that existed before the first word. His eyes show the beginning and end of all timelines converging in a single moment, and his voice is not heard but felt in the vibration of reality itself. Around him, the cosmos unravels and reknits itself in endless cycles, demonstrating that he is not merely a god but the canvas upon which all gods are painted.
supreme_god.lore: In the time before time, when existence was only a single thought in the infinite mind of nothingness, Olodumare-No-Hasshin awoke. Not created, not born, but simply was—the first consciousness that recognized itself. From that self-awareness flowed Ashe, the divine life-force that would become all things. He is the Unmoved Mover, the Source Without Source, who exists in Orun (heaven) while his emanations—the Orishas—manage Ayé (earth). Ancient texts say he created the universe not with hands or words, but by contemplating its possibility so deeply that it had no choice but to manifest. He established the 256 Odus (destiny patterns) before creating the first soul, ensuring that free will and destiny could dance together without stepping on each other's feet. He is so supreme that he cannot be worshipped directly—mortals must approach through his Orishas, who are his hands, voice, and heart in the material world.
supreme_god.appearance: Has no visible form - represented by pure white light or complete darkness. When manifesting, appears as ancient elder of indeterminate gender with skin like night sky full of stars.

unique_abilities.name: Ayanmo (Divine Destiny)
unique_abilities.effect: Can set the fundamental destiny/purpose of any being or thing, which cannot be altered except by his will
unique_abilities.cooldown: Only at creation or re-creation

unique_abilities.name: Ashe Infusion
unique_abilities.effect: Can grant or withdraw the divine life-force that powers all magic and existence in the Shattered Expanse
unique_abilities.cooldown: Through cosmic intermediaries only

supreme_god.current_role: Maintaining the fundamental existence of reality, overseeing the balance of Ashe throughout all realms.
duties: Sustaining the cosmic balance between Orun (heaven) and Ayé (earth)
Assigning primordial destinies to all created beings
Regulating the flow of Ashe through cosmic channels
Appointing and empowering Orishas to manage specific domains
supreme_god.ascension_story: Not ascended; is the primordial consciousness that preceded existence itself. Emerged from the 'Great Unthinking' when possibility first differentiated from impossibility.
sacred_items: The Calabash of Existence (contains all potential realities)
Divine Palm Nuts (used to cast the first destiny patterns)
White Cloth of Purity (represents his untouched nature)

allies: All Orishas (as his children and extensions)
rivals: Forces of absolute nothingness (which seek to uncreate)
creations: All existence in the Shattered Expanse

weaknesses: Cannot interact directly with creation without destroying it (must work through Orishas)
Bound by the cosmic laws he established
Cannot act against destiny once it is set
Requires intermediaries for any action in the material world
supreme_god.realm: Orun (The invisible heaven beyond the Expanse)
supreme_god.temples: None - too supreme for temples, worshipped through Orishas

high_gods.name: Obatala-No-Jozu, The King of White Cloth
high_gods.title: Creator of Human Forms
high_gods.god_of: Orisha who shapes human bodies from clay. Represents coolness, patience, and purity. Father of all Orishas and humanity.
high_gods.description: Obatala-No-Jozu manifests as a being of pristine white light and serene perfection, his form sculpted from living alabaster and moonlight, towering with the calm authority of a divine sculptor. His skin is polished white porcelain that reflects purity, his eyes are deep wells of tranquil wisdom holding galaxies of unborn souls awaiting form, and his hair flows like cascading fresh water. He wears robes of woven peace and carries the Iroke Staff that can separate chaos from order. At his feet, the clay of creation waits to be shaped, and around him float the perfect geometric forms of potential humanity. His aura is the cool, clear morning of the first day, bringing clarity, peace, and perfect form to all chaos.
high_gods.lore: When Olodumare-No-Hasshin first contemplated physical forms, Obatala-No-Jozu emerged from that thought as the divine sculptor. He descended to the primordial swamp with a bag of sacred clay and a calabash of cool water from Orun. For seven days and seven nights, he shaped the first humans, breathing life into them only when their forms were perfect. He is known for his patience—once spending a century perfecting a single eyelid—and his commitment to purity. When he drinks palm wine (his one weakness), his creations become flawed, which is why some humans are born with disabilities. Out of remorse, he became their special protector. He mediates disputes among Orishas with calm wisdom, and his white garments never stain, symbolizing his uncorrupted nature.
high_gods.appearance: Ancient yet ageless male figure with skin like polished alabaster, white hair and beard, eyes like deep still water. Always dressed in immaculate white robes. Carries the Iroke staff and a bag of creation clay.
high_gods.ascension_story: First among the Orishas created by Olodumare-No-Hasshin to manifest physical reality. Emerged fully formed from Olodumare's contemplation of form and order.

unique_abilities.name: Iwa-Pele (Good Character)
unique_abilities.effect: Can instill moral excellence and peaceful nature in any being
unique_abilities.cooldown: Requires the being's willingness to change

unique_abilities.name: Clay of Creation
unique_abilities.effect: Can shape living beings from sacred earth and divine breath
unique_abilities.cooldown: One creation per lunar cycle

unique_abilities.name: Coolness of Mind
unique_abilities.effect: Can calm any conflict, rage, or chaotic situation through sheer presence
unique_abilities.cooldown: Continuous while present

high_gods.current_role: Supreme sculptor of mortal forms, peacemaker among Orishas, protector of the disabled.
duties: Shaping physical bodies for newborn souls
Mediating conflicts between other Orishas
Maintaining purity in sacred spaces
Protecting those born with disabilities
sacred_items: The Iroke Staff (separates order from chaos)
Bag of Creation Clay (infinite sacred earth)
Calabash of Orun Water (purifies all it touches)

rivals: Shango-No-Inazuma (hot temper vs his cool nature)
creations: The first cities and their orderly layouts

weaknesses: Becomes careless and flawed when drinking palm wine
Cannot tolerate impurity in his immediate presence
Bound to protect even flawed creations
Powerless against willful, chaotic evil that refuses negotiation

high_gods.name: Yemoja-No-Umi, Mother of Fishes
high_gods.title: Goddess of the Living Ocean
high_gods.god_of: Mother of all Orishas, goddess whose womb is the ocean. Protector of women and children. Her tears become rivers.
high_gods.description: Yemoja-No-Umi rises from the ocean depths as a goddess of maternal majesty, her form a fusion of woman and living sea, skin the shifting colors of tropical waters from turquoise to deep indigo, hair flowing with schools of glowing fish and strands of pearls. Her eyes hold the depth of ocean trenches and the warmth of sun-warmed shallows, her body both voluptuous mother and powerful wave. She wears garments of living coral and sea-foam lace, with a necklace of cowrie shells that whisper ocean secrets. Water births from her hands, forming rivers that flow backward to their source, and her aura is the soothing, amniotic embrace of primal waters that nurture all life.
high_gods.lore: Yemoja-No-Umi was the first consciousness to emerge from water when Olodumare-No-Hasshin breathed life into the primordial seas. She is the Great Mother who birthed many Orishas from her watery womb and adopted others as her own. When the first humans struggled on land, she sent rivers inland so they would never be far from her nurturing embrace. Her love is vast as the ocean but fierce as a tsunami when her children are threatened. She collects the tears of all suffering beings in her oceanic heart, purifying them and returning them as life-giving rain. Sailors tell of her appearing as a mermaid to guide lost ships, and mothers pray to her during childbirth for safe delivery.
high_gods.appearance: A majestic woman with skin the color of deep ocean waters, hair of flowing seaweed and pearls, wearing a dress of living coral and shells. Always surrounded by water and marine life.
high_gods.ascension_story: Emerged naturally when the first seas gained consciousness from Olodumare's Ashe. Grew in power as life evolved in her waters, becoming mother to all aquatic creatures and eventually to many Orishas.

unique_abilities.name: Omi Tutu (Cool Water)
unique_abilities.effect: Her waters can calm any storm, physical or emotional
unique_abilities.cooldown: Tidal cycle based

unique_abilities.name: Womb of Life
unique_abilities.effect: Can grant fertility to barren beings or places
unique_abilities.cooldown: Seasonal, aligned with lunar cycles

unique_abilities.name: Maternal Embrace
unique_abilities.effect: Can create protective barriers of water that only she can penetrate
unique_abilities.cooldown: Duration depends on emotional connection

high_gods.current_role: Mother-protector of all life, guardian of women and children, queen of the oceans.
duties: Nurturing all newborn life (aquatic and terrestrial)
Protecting women during childbirth
Regulating ocean currents and tides
Comforting the grieving with her eternal embrace
sacred_items: The Cowrie Necklace (whispers ocean secrets)
Mother's Calabash (provides endless nourishing water)
Pearl of Tears (stores and purifies sorrow)
weaknesses: Cannot bear to see any child suffer (must intervene)
Power diminishes in deserts and arid places
Bound by maternal love even toward ungrateful children
Vulnerable to water pollution and poisoning

high_gods.name: Shango-No-Inazuma, King of Thunder
high_gods.title: Lord of Lightning and Justice
high_gods.god_of: Orisha of thunder who wields double-headed axe. Represents masculine power, dance, and justice. Former king of Oyo.
high_gods.description: Shango-No-Inazuma manifests as a storm given royal form, a muscular god of crackling energy and regal wrath, skin the color of storm clouds at sunset, eyes flashing with lightning bolts, hair a wild mane of electricity and smoke. He wears royal red and white garments that ripple with thunder, holds the double-headed Oshe axe that channels celestial fire, and dances with steps that shake mountains. His voice is rolling thunder that speaks judgment, and his laughter is the sharp crack of lightning that purifies.
